This role will lead sales and use tax strategy across product launches, business initiatives, compliance, audits, and tax operations, while partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, and Operations. The role reports directly to the Director of Tax. As an early member of the tax team, you will play a critical role in shaping Whop’s approach to sales and use taxation across existing and emerging business models. You will evaluate complex digital commerce transactions, advise on marketplace facilitator and platform tax issues, support nexus and taxability analyses, and help build scalable processes and systems that support rapid growth. This position sits at the intersection of tax, technology, and operations, offering a unique opportunity to influence product design, automate tax processes, and establish best-in-class indirect tax practices within a high-growth technology company. On-site work at the Palo Alto office is currently required on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays. What You'll Do Own U.S. sales and use tax compliance Lead U.S. sales and use tax compliance across all applicable state and local jurisdictions, including manage nexus analyses, registrations, return filings, reconciliations, and compliance monitoring. Monitor legislative and regulatory developments and assess their impact on Whop's products, services, and operations. Lead Product Taxability Analysis Evaluate the sales and use tax treatment of new products, features, services, and business initiatives. Partner with Product, Engineering, and Legal teams throughout the product development lifecycle to ensure tax requirements are considered early and implemented effectively. Develop and Document Tax Positions Establish, maintain, and periodically review formal sales and use tax position documentation. One-pagers, battle cards, outbound templates, email sequences. Work with GTM Associates to make sure every word hitting enterprise inboxes is persona-specific and on-brand Who you are: - You think in programs, not just pieces. A blog post isn't a blog post. It's part of a campaign. - You can make complex technology feel simple without dumbing it down. Think Apple, not enterprise jargon. - You write for different personas and buying stages without losing the brand thread. Customer service leaders and CIOs need different messages, but both should feel like Zowie. - You're opinionated about brand voice and not afraid to push back when something doesn't sound right. - You can move between a homepage headline, a webinar concept, and a 50-word outbound email without switching gears. - You use AI tools fluently for research, drafting, and production. Nice to have: - Experience at a challenger or category-creating brand - Background in AI, automation, or customer experience - Experience producing webinars or digital events - Familiarity with tools like HubSpot, Webflow, or similar - A portfolio that shows range (web copy, long-form, campaigns, email) AI-native culture Our team embraces AI as a fundamental part of how we work. You set the direction, shape the output, and ensure everything meets the bar. The result is one person with the output of a small team and the strategic thinking the brand actually needs.

We work with the Department of War to provide the high-speed capabilities our nation and its allies need to maintain a durable, asymmetric advantage.
